proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved an exact necessary-and-sufficient pullback criterion for aligned finite real-kernel causal abstractions, with a forced paired-state carrier, a universal mediator, and explicit ambiguity/support-hole nonexistence certificates. A bounded repair made the exact-table algorithm honest about promised aligned rational inputs, removed unsupported polynomial complexity, and synchronized universal terminality over all finite real source cones; both final panels passed. The result nevertheless remained incremental and below the field floor because the aligned topology is narrower than the anchor's general-node-map setting; a field-level continuation would require genuinely new nonaligned theory or a substantive application.
tldr: For two finite real-kernel causal Bayesian networks abstracting to the same ordered coarse model through identical bijective node maps but possibly lossy state maps, a pullback exists exactly when every pinned local fixed-margin coupling is unique and the supports of those unique free-node responses, together with pairs forced by coordinatewise surjectivity, cover every compatible paired state. The pullback is the explicit paired-state CBN \(P^\times\), and every finite real-kernel source cone has the unique componentwise-pair mediator. Failure of coupling uniqueness or coverage yields two finite real cones with no common receiver. For explicitly tabulated rational cospans already known to be valid aligned causal abstractions, the same criterion gives a finite exact rational decision and certificate procedure; no polynomial operation or time bound is claimed.
gap: The founding \(\mathsf{CM}_{\mathrm{abs}}\) paper proves pullback existence under a bijective-side condition and explicitly identifies precise necessary conditions as its most important open problem. Its lossy-state counterexample shows ambiguity but does not classify when two genuinely lossy aligned abstractions can still be merged or certify failure against every possible terminal cone.
fill: Prove an iff theorem, not merely another sufficient construction: derive the local transportation criterion, show support coverage is exactly what makes every forced mediator surjective, lift co-singleton identities to all interventions and reflected edges, and turn each failed condition into two explicit cones with no common receiver. Add an exact expanded-table recognition and certificate procedure.
